disclosure: Disclosure: battleships.dev, cited in this document, is built by the Boat team; Boat is one of the providers compared here. It is used as a cross-check, never as the sole source of a rate or verdict.

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go — Tier 0
plans.includedUsage: Up to $200 in promotional credits; exact grant per account is not published.
plans.retentionQuote: Some quota tiers enforce expiration dates (Tier 0 and 1, with respectively up to 7 and 30 days).
plans.sessionQuote: Sandboxes are built for workloads lasting anywhere from a few seconds to multiple days.
plans.notes: No per-tier sandbox size cap is published. Battleships lists a 2 vCPU / 4 GiB cap that it says was not re-verified; see diffs.

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go — Tier 1
plans.includedUsage: The $20 is a wallet top-up, not a fee; it becomes usage credit.
plans.notes: Tier is set by 30-day top-up volume and can drop if top-ups stop.

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go — Tier 2
plans.includedUsage: The $50 is a wallet top-up, not a fee; it becomes usage credit.
plans.notes: Tiers 3-8 are not published; the pricing page jumps from Tier 2 to Tier 9.

plans.name: Custom
plans.quote: Up to 256 GB RAM per sandbox or job
plans.notes: Quote-only: private networking, bring-your-own-metal, custom SLAs and hardware.

compute.billingBasis: Allocated memory × active seconds. CPU is allocated from the memory size and is not billed separately.

floor.detail: No minimum billed duration or minimum memory charge is published.
floor.quote: billed by its allocated memory (CPU scales automatically)

increment.detail: The rate is per GB-second and billing is reported in GB-seconds.

perResourceRates.quote: CPU resources are allocated accordingly by Blaxel based on your selected memory allocation and are not charged separately.

fixedSizes.name: 8 GB sandbox
fixedSizes.quote: a sandbox with 8 GB memory is allocated 4 CPU cores, while one with 16 GB memory is allocated 6 CPU cores
fixedSizes.notes: Price derived from 8 GB × 3,600 s × $0.0000115; no disk is included because the writable layer is tmpfs in RAM.

fixedSizes.name: 16 GB sandbox
fixedSizes.quote: a sandbox with 8 GB memory is allocated 4 CPU cores, while one with 16 GB memory is allocated 6 CPU cores

compute.notes: Blaxel publishes no per-vCPU price. Because CPU scales with RAM, a bigger sandbox buys more cores at the same per-GB rate. Batch jobs ($0.000006/GB-s) and MCP hosting ($0.000007/GB-s) are separate products.

disk.detail: The writable filesystem lives in RAM as tmpfs, roughly 50% of allocated memory, so there is no separate local-disk charge. Persistent disk is a Volume.
disk.quote: a writable layer lives entirely in the sandbox's RAM using `tmpfs`

billedWhileStopped.model: snapshot storage plus any attached volume
billedWhileStopped.quote: You are charged only for snapshot and volume storage
billedWhileStopped.overviewQuote: You are not charged for memory while a sandbox is in standby mode. However, you are charged for the storage of the snapshot and/or the volumes.

snapshotStorage.notes: The pricing table labels this 'Snapshots storage — Memory and filesystem snapshots that keep suspended sandboxes ready to resume.' No statement of whether the billable size is allocated RAM, written bytes, or both.

volumes.billedOn: provisioned capacity, whether or not written
volumes.provisionedQuote: Billed on the volume size you provision, for as long as the volume exists, regardless of how much data you actually write in it.

retention.stoppedDataKept: Standby has no expiry on higher tiers; Tier 0 caps sandbox lifetime at 7 days and Tier 1 at 30 days. Without a TTL or lifecycle policy, sandboxes are not deleted.
retention.quote: If these parameters are absent, sandboxes will not be deleted.
retention.indefiniteQuote: sandboxes wait on standby indefinitely when not used

egress.quote: Internet egress traffic | Outbound traffic from your workloads to the internet. | Included
egress.notes: The pricing table lists outbound internet traffic as 'Included'. Dedicated egress IPs, gateway runtime and proxy data are 'Free during beta'.

other.notes: Workspace roles are admin, member and viewer, but no per-user or per-seat price appears on the pricing page.

freeTier.type: promotional credits plus a free tier
freeTier.limits: Up to $200 in free credits; Tier 0 allows 10 concurrent sandboxes and caps sandbox lifetime at 7 days.
freeTier.notes: 'Up to' is the only published figure; the actual grant per account and what happens at exhaustion are not documented on the pricing page.

diffs.ours: No per-tier sandbox size cap was published; custom plans go to 256 GB RAM.
diffs.battleships: Tier 0 max 2 vCPU / 4 GiB, sizes 2 GB and 4 GB, flagged as not re-verified.
diffs.live: Still no per-tier size table; the pricing page says to view all tiers in the console and lists only sandbox counts.

diffs.ours: Described Tier 1 and Tier 2 as $20/month and $50/month.
diffs.battleships: Encodes fee 20 and 50 but marks fee_is_credit true.
diffs.live: Treats the Tier 1 and Tier 2 amounts as top-ups deposited into the wallet rather than as fees.
diffs.quote: Funds added to meet a tier requirement are deposited directly into your account balance.

diffs.ours: Flagged a conflict: the pricing FAQ says about 5 seconds, the sandbox docs say about 15 seconds.
diffs.battleships: Keeps 15 seconds and notes the 5-second claim.
diffs.live: Both claims are still live on their respective pages, so the conflict is unresolved.
diffs.quote: Sandboxes scale to zero after about 5 seconds of inactivity and resume from standby in roughly 25ms

diffs.ours: Per-second metering implied by the per-GB-second rate.
diffs.battleships: Minimum billed seconds per resume listed as undocumented.
diffs.live: The billing doc states compute runtime charges are measured in GB-seconds, which confirms sub-minute metering but not a minimum increment.

diffs.ours: $0.20/GB-month with the billable size not established.
diffs.battleships: Assumes the billable snapshot size is roughly allocated memory (2 GB standby for a month = $0.40).
diffs.live: Neither the pricing page nor the standby doc says whether the GB figure is allocated RAM, written bytes, or both.

isolation.title: Run sandbox workloads as a non-root user

manualRoute: Create a sandbox with the Blaxel CLI or Python SDK and open a preview URL on the agent's port.
Connect to the sandbox terminal (bl connect sandbox) and install the agent with npm or its installer.
Run the agent's onboarding, attach a Volume for persistence, and set a TTL or lifecycle policy.

evidence.claim: Blaxel publishes an official OpenClaw walkthrough, and it is explicitly a manual install.
evidence.quote: OpenClaw can be manually installed and configured to run inside a Blaxel sandbox.

evidence.claim: The walkthrough needs a terminal, Python, the CLI and a model-provider key.
Agents Hosting, the managed agent product, caps a run at 15 minutes and so is not an always-on home for a personal agent.
evidence.quote: Agents deployed on Blaxel Agents Hosting have a maximum runtime of 15 minutes.

evidence.claim: Preview URLs can be created from the Console, which is the one useful no-terminal step.
evidence.quote: You can create a preview URL for a sandbox from the Blaxel Console

deploy.notes: No Hermes Agent guide or template was found in Blaxel's documentation index. The OpenClaw guide is a developer tutorial, not a one-click deploy: it assumes a terminal, a Python environment and a model API key. A non-coder can create a sandbox and a preview URL in the console but cannot install or configure the agent there.
